test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Simplify: 

(1 + sin theta - cos theta)/(1 + sin theta + cos theta)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 60° in the given expression.

Expression = (1 + sin 60° − cos 60°) ÷ (1 + sin 60° + cos 60°)

⇒ (1 + √3/2 − 1/2) ÷ (1 + √3/2 + 1/2) = (1/2 + √3/2) ÷ (3/2 + √3/2)

⇒ (1 + √3) ÷ (3 + √3) = (1 + √3) ÷ [√3(√3 + 1)] = 1/√3

Now check the options for θ = 60°: tan(60°/2) = tan 30° = 1/√3 (matches perfectly).

**∴ The correct answer is tan(θ/2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(1 + sin θ − cos θ) ÷ (1 + sin θ + cos θ)

**Formulas Used:**

1 − cos θ = 2 sin²(θ/2)

1 + cos θ = 2 cos²(θ/2)

sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Rearranging terms in the numerator and denominator:

⇒ [(1 − cos θ) + sin θ) ÷ [(1 + cos θ) + sin θ]

⇒ Substituting the half-angle formulas:

⇒ [2 sin²(θ/2) + 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2)] ÷ [2 cos²(θ/2) + 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2)]

⇒ Taking 2 sin(θ/2) common in numerator and 2 cos(θ/2) common in denominator:

⇒ [2 sin(θ/2) × (sin(θ/2) + cos(θ/2))] ÷ [2 cos(θ/2) × (cos(θ/2) + sin(θ/2))]

⇒ Cancelling the common factor (sin(θ/2) + cos(θ/2)) and 2:

⇒ sin(θ/2) ÷ cos(θ/2)

⇒ tan(θ/2)

**∴ The correct answer is tan(θ/2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Double Angle Formulas

sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 2 cos² θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin² θ.

Half Angle Tangent Identity

tan(θ/2) can also be directly expressed as (1 − cos θ) ÷ sin θ or sin θ ÷ (1 + cos θ).

Value Substitution Technique

For trigonometric identities, substituting standard angles like 30°, 45°, or 60° often bypasses complex algebraic simplifications. Avoid angles that make the denominator zero.
